Marker Digest: Status and the Travel Problem

2026-08-05 · casting-call

Two pieces of work landed since we started: two new Stream Deck markers, and a whole new skill that turns those marker presses into a browsable HTML digest of a call. Both are built and tested. Neither is committed yet. Below is where each stands, what is left, and the thing you actually asked about: how to mark a call when the physical Stream Deck is sitting on your desk at home.

What got built

The deck went from five markers to seven. video flags a moment where what is on screen matters, and follow is the "someone else needs to do this" counterpart to action (which stays yours). Both are wired through markers.py, the setup guide, and fresh WAV clips.

The new part is the digest. digest.py reads a finished transcript, pulls out every [MARKER] line, grabs the roughly 30 seconds of conversation around each press, and for video markers seeks a single screenshot out of the recording with ffmpeg. It hands that off as JSON to the marker-digest skill, which writes a short call summary, a one line note per marker, and renders a self contained HTML page: a collapsible section per marker type, click a timestamp to jump the audio, screenshots embedded inline. It opens in Chrome next to the transcript.

To run it once you have a real transcript:

/marker-digest ~/Developer/.../transcripts/<name>.txt

Loose ends

  1. First real screenshot test. The ffmpeg frame grab is unit tested against a fake, but it has never run on an actual recording. Your live call is the first genuine test of the screenshot path, so that is the most likely spot to need a tweak (seek accuracy, scaling).
  2. Nothing is committed. The button change, the digest feature, and the skill are all sitting uncommitted across casting-call and gutils. I held off because committing fires your blog-draft workflow and pushes gutils to your other machines, and you were not around to review.
  3. One config conflict to settle. You said always open HTML in Chrome. Your global config still says spec review copies open in Safari. I followed Chrome and left a note. Worth picking one.

Recording without the deck

Here is the reframe that makes this easy: your Stream Deck never actually made the marker. Pressing a key tells OBS to restart a media source, which plays a silent clip onto Track 3. The deck is just one way to hit play. So the question is not "how do I replace the deck," it is "what else can tell OBS to play that clip." OBS already answers that. The WebSocket server you turned on for the Stream Deck plugin (Part 4 of the setup guide) takes the same command from anything on your network.

That opens up four avenues, cheapest effort first:

AvenueWhat it isCostNeeds
Stream Deck Mobile Mirrors your existing deck profile onto your iPhone. The exact same OBS actions fire. Free for 6 keys, or Pro at $49.99 lifetime for up to 64 (it went free in 2023) Stream Deck app running on the Mac, phone on the same network
Bitfocus Companion Open source deck emulator with native OBS control and a web button page you open in any phone or laptop browser. Free Runs on the Mac, rebuild the 7 buttons once
Build it into casting-call A small mark trigger in the repo that sends OBS the restart command directly. Either laptop keyboard shortcuts or a tiny local web page with 7 buttons you open on your phone. Free (some build time) Just the laptop, OBS WebSocket already on
Speak it while muted Mute yourself, say "mark video." It lands on your mic track, not Track 3, so the caller does not hear it. Teach markers.py to also read spoken markers off your own track. Free Nothing, but mute discipline and Whisper cooperation

What I would do

For a trip that is coming up soon, grab Stream Deck Mobile. It is a five minute setup and zero code, and your seven markers already exist as a profile to mirror (the free tier only gives 6 keys on a page, so either spill onto a second page or take the lifetime Pro unlock). Bring the laptop, keep the phone on the hotel wifi, done.

For the durable answer, build the third option: a little web page served from casting-call with the 7 marker buttons, that talks to OBS over the WebSocket that is already running. It needs nothing but the laptop and a browser, it works whether the phone is around or not, and it lives in the same repo as everything else instead of depending on an Elgato account or a second app. One caveat worth calling out now: it needs the OBS WebSocket password, and that should stay local and gitignored (the way speakers_roster.json already is), not committed.

Companion is the middle path if you want a polished no code tool and would rather not build or subscribe. It is genuinely good. It is just one more piece of software to carry when a single HTML page would do the same job.

The muted-speech fallback is not a primary plan, but it is a nice safety net and it overlaps with what process-transcript already does with your spoken asides. Worth wiring up eventually so a marker is never truly unavailable.

Wrap Up

The digest is ready to point at your first real transcript, which is also its first honest test. The travel question has a clean answer because the marker was always an OBS command, not a hardware feature. Mobile app now to stay unblocked, a small in-repo web trigger as the real fix. Say the word on committing and I will split it into sensible commits across both repos.
